title: Chitlin-circuit one-nighters and a racial insult in Goldsboro
summary: Three months without a night off on the black circuit, and a hostess announcing 'a hot nigger band' in Goldsboro, North Carolina.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And we used to have, like a string of one nighters, three straight months without a night off -- I mean we played all of the chitlin circuits, we used to call them, because it was all black dancers, all except maybe one or two white dancers who were thrown in on a Saturday night.

I never will forget in Goldsboro, North Carolina -- naturally I was the first one in, setting up, and (UNINTELLIGIBLE) was setting my drums up for me and I came to check to see whether they were set up right.

And this white couple came to the door and they wanted to know who was playing that night, and the hostess, the lady who was doing the seating, came and said, 'Oh, we got a hot nigger band tonite -- Lucky Millinder, they're gonna play some hot music for us'.
That was quite apres-pos, wasn't it?
Oh yeah. And I sat there with my mouth open, because you know, it was sort of a shock to me,
